insights.concise_text: The framework's conversational flow patterns are evaluated on 108 IQ2 debates whose winners are defined by pre- and post-debate audience vote deltas.

triple.subject: conversational flow patterns
triple.object: 108 IQ2 debates with pre- and post-debate audience vote deltas

insights.concise_text: Oxford-style debates disentangle conversational flow effects from audience prior leaning because the audience votes before and after the debate.

triple.subject: pre- and post-debate audience voting
triple.object: disentangling conversational flow effects from audience prior leaning

insights.concise_text: The opening statement that enables identifying pre-interaction talking points is instantiated in IQ2 by 7 minutes for each debater to lay out main points.

triple.subject: opening statement
triple.object: 7 minutes for each debater to lay out their main points

insights.concise_text: Talking points identified from introduction word-usage divergence become the basis for self-coverage and opponent-coverage measured during the discussion.

triple.subject: talking points from introduction word-usage divergence
triple.object: self-coverage and opponent-coverage during the discussion

insights.concise_text: The observed larger drop in self-coverage for eventual winners supports the claim that debaters benefit by shifting away from introduction-salient talking points.

triple.subject: larger drop in self-coverage for eventual winners
triple.object: benefit from shifting away from introduction-salient talking points

insights.concise_text: The finding that eventual winners adopt more opponent-introduced discussion points is interpreted as contesting opponents' points, supported by 78% of valid discussion points being picked up to be challenged.

triple.subject: eventual winners adopting more opponent-introduced discussion points
triple.object: interpretation as contesting opponents' points

insights.concise_text: Flow features include the number of discussion points adopted, and Flow* selects that feature most often with positive regression coefficients.

triple.subject: number of discussion points adopted
triple.object: Flow features into a positively weighted Flow* feature

insights.concise_text: Using leave-one-out evaluation with logistic regression, Flow features reach 63% and Flow* reaches 65%, outperforming the 50% random baseline.

triple.subject: Flow and Flow*
triple.object: 50% random baseline

insights.concise_text: Audience features use applause and laughter counts, whose observed relation to debate outcome supports treating them as rough indicators of how well the audience can foresee a debate's outcome.

triple.subject: applause and laughter counts
triple.object: rough indicators of how well the audience can foresee a debate's outcome

insights.concise_text: The basic unigram-based definition of discussion points limits idea flow analysis robustness because it does not account for context or semantic sense.

triple.subject: basic unigram-based definition of discussion points
triple.object: robustness of idea flow analysis
